skill.name: handoff
skill.description: Create a concise handoff document so another AI agent can continue the current work.
skill.summary: Create a focused handoff note for continuing work in another AI session.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: The static findings point to line 7, where the prompt asks the agent to create a temp Markdown file using a mktemp command. Both findings are false positives because the command is hardcoded, creates the intended output location, and does not use user-controlled shell input. No semantic prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: Write a handoff document summarising the current conversation so a fresh agent can continue the work
Write a handoff document summarising the current conversation so a fresh agent can continue the work

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 7 contains a Markdown-inline mktemp command with fixed arguments, not Ruby or shell backtick execution in code. It creates an intended temporary output path and has no user-controlled shell interpolation.
Line 7 intentionally asks for a temporary Markdown handoff file, which is the skill's expected output. The path is generated by mktemp, with no destructive operation or arbitrary path input.

content.value_statement: Agent handoffs often lose context, decisions, and next steps between sessions. This skill creates a concise handoff note so Claude, Codex, or Claude Code can continue the work.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes the current conversation into a handoff document.
Saves the handoff to a temporary Markdown file.
Suggests relevant skills for the next session.
References existing artifacts instead of duplicating their content.
Tailors the handoff to user-supplied focus details.
limitations: It depends on the current agent having enough conversation context.
It does not inspect unrelated files unless the agent chooses to reference them.
It creates a local temporary file and does not manage long-term storage.
It is not a project management system or issue tracker.

use_cases.title: Transfer Implementation Context
use_cases.description: A developer ends a long coding session and needs the next agent to continue without repeating analysis.

use_cases.title: Preserve Decision Context
use_cases.description: A team lead wants a short record of decisions, constraints, and references before assigning follow-up work.

use_cases.title: Resume Investigation Work
use_cases.description: A support engineer needs another session to continue an issue investigation with clear status and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: End a simple session with a clear continuation note.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the handoff skill for this session. Focus on the main goal, completed work, and the next recommended step.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Bug Fix Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Transfer debugging work to another AI session.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the handoff skill for the current debugging session. Include failing symptoms, files reviewed, tests run, and unresolved questions.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Multi-Agent Project
prompt_templates.scenario: Keep project context concise across several sessions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the handoff skill for the current project. Reference existing plans, issues, commits, and diffs instead of repeating them.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Targeted Continuation Brief
prompt_templates.scenario: Guide the next session toward a specific implementation goal.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the handoff skill with this focus: next session should implement the API changes. Include constraints, risks, and verification steps.

output_examples.input: Prepare a handoff for finishing the authentication bug fix.
output_examples.output: A concise Markdown handoff saved to a temporary file. It lists current status, reviewed files, failing tests, next actions, and open questions.

output_examples.input: Create a handoff focused on the next product planning session.
output_examples.output: A planning-focused handoff that references existing documents, summarizes decisions, and names the most important follow-up questions.

output_examples.input: Summarize this session so Claude Code can continue the refactor.
output_examples.output: A continuation note with refactor goals, changed files, validation status, unresolved risks, and suggested skills for the next session.

best_practices: Run the skill near the end of a session, after important decisions are clear.
Pass a clear focus when the next session has a specific goal.
Keep durable project details in source files, issues, or plans, then reference them.
anti_patterns: Using the handoff as the only record for long-term project decisions.
Including secrets, credentials, or private customer data in the handoff.
Requesting a handoff before the session has enough useful context.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a concise Markdown handoff document for another AI agent or session.

faq.question: Where does the handoff file go?
faq.answer: The skill asks the agent to save it as a temporary Markdown file using mktemp.

faq.question: Can I give the next session a focus?
faq.answer: Yes. Pass a short focus description, and the handoff should be tailored to that goal.

faq.question: Does it duplicate project documents?
faq.answer: No. The skill tells the agent to reference existing artifacts instead of duplicating their content.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks the skill as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Should handoffs include secrets?
faq.answer: No. Avoid secrets, tokens, customer data, and other sensitive details in handoff notes.
